previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent ER-positive breast cancer and idiopathic gastroparesis presented with a severe flare of nausea, vomiting, and epigastric pain. Initial evaluation revealed hypovolemia and metabolic abnormalities consistent with starvation ketosis, which resolved with IV hydration and supportive care. A CT scan showed new hepatic and skeletal lesions suspicious for metastatic disease, prompting a percutaneous liver biopsy. She was managed for gastroparesis with antiemetics and dietary advancement, and a UTI with E. coli was incidentally detected and treated. The Denosumab was held pending oncology review. She improved clinically, tolerated a regular diet, and was discharged home with plans to follow up with her oncologist for biopsy results and further management.
problems: Secondary malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile duct
Malignant neoplasm of unspecified site of unspecified female breast

Her breast cancer history began in ___ when she developed a

reexcision, she had breast conserving radiation administered at
___. She had no adjuvant systemic therapy.

In ___, a mammogram showed right breast 
microcalcifications
which were stable. These were in the retroareolar area. On the
left side, however, she had an asymmetry. This was superior and
posterior aspect of the breast and an ultrasound was performed
showing an ill-defined hypoechoic mass measuring about 1 cm. She
had a core biopsy of this area in ___. Pathology revealed
malignancy, so she underwent a left mastectomy, having had a
prior excision and radiation therapy on the left side. Final
surgical pathology showed invasive lobular cancer measuring 13
mm. This was histologic grade II. There was a single focus of
invasion. There was no lymphovascular invasion. Both hormone
receptors were positive while HER-2/neu was negative by
immunohistochemistry.  No lymph nodes were sampled given the
prior lower axillary dissection.

Her Oncotype recurrence score was 20. This corresponds to a 13%
___ risk of recurrence assuming ___ years of tamoxifen. We
would expect somewhat better results for management of lobular
carcinoma with an aromatase inhibitor. On the other hand, this
was apparently recurrent disease after prior radiation therapy,
which might have diminished tumor sensitivity to additional
therapy.

We discussed adjuvant treatment, both endocrine therapy and
chemo-endocrine therapy. She favored endocrine therapy alone
strongly and I felt this was an acceptable choice. Accordingly,
anastrozole was started in ___.

She recently presented to the ED on ___ with nausea,
vomiting, and abdominal pain. This was felt to be related to her
gastroparesis. Her CT abdomen/pelvis returned consistent with
numerous hepatic and osseous metastases. In the hospital, she
underwent a liver biopsy which revealed a carcinoma compatible
with a breast primary tumor. Estrogen receptor was positive. 
HER-2/neu was not assessed.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ y/o woman with metastatic breast cancer (to 
liver and spine), chronic cancer-associated pain, and 
gastroparesis, who presented with back pain and urinary 
incontinence. She has had progression of disease on anastrozole, 
and her metastases were recently discovered. On presentation, 
she underwent MRI of the spine, which demonstrated diffuse 
osseous metastases, but no evidence of spinal cord compression. 
She was evaluated by radiation oncology, who noted that given 
the diffuse nature of her spinal disease, systemic therapy would 
be more beneficial than radiotherapy. Her pain was well 
controlled with her home MSContin and Dilaudid. Bowel regimen 
added given chronic opioid use. She was treated with ceftriaxone 
for UTI, which was switched to PO cefpodoxime. She will complete 
a 7 day course on ___. She is scheduled for port placement 
on ___ and will have oncology follow up for potential 
initiation of chemotherapy. She was otherwise continued on her 
home omeprazole, citalopram, lorazepam, and levothyroxine.
